statement: Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. Given that the product of the two numbers is even, what is the probability that their sum is $7$?

choices.misconception: I multiplied P(sum 7) = 1/6 by P(product even) = 3/4 instead of dividing by P(product even).
I ignored the given information and gave the ordinary probability that the sum is 7.
I assumed half of the 36 outcomes, 18, have an even product, and divided the 6 outcomes with sum 7 by 18.
I swapped the condition and found the probability that the product is even given that the sum is 7.

hints: Shrink the sample space to the outcomes with an even product.
Count the outcomes with an even product using the complement (both dice odd). Then count how many of those also have sum 7, and divide.
Even product: $36 - 9 = 27$ outcomes. Every sum-$7$ outcome has one odd and one even die, so all $6$ of them have an even product.

solutions.reliable: Of the $36$ equally likely outcomes, the product is odd only when both dice are odd: $3 \cdot 3 = 9$ outcomes. So $27$ outcomes have an even product, and they form the new sample space. A sum of $7$ is odd, so one die is odd and the other is even, which makes the product even. Hence all $6$ outcomes with sum $7$, namely $(1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1)$, lie inside the $27$. The probability is $6/27 = 2/9$. Transferable idea: a conditional probability is a count inside the smaller sample space.
solutions.elegant: $P(\text{sum } 7 \mid \text{even product}) = \dfrac{P(\text{sum } 7 \text{ and even product})}{P(\text{even product})} = \dfrac{1/6}{3/4} = \dfrac{2}{9}$, because a sum of $7$ already forces an even product.
